'''''Xanthium spinosum''''' (also known as ''Acanthoxanthium spinosum'') is a species of flowering plant in the [[Asteraceae|aster family]] known by many common names, including '''spiny cocklebur''', '''prickly burweed''' and '''Bathurst burr'''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bathurst Burr|publisher=Department of Primary Industries|url=http://www.dpi.vic.gov.au/agriculture/pests-diseases-and-weeds/weeds/other-declared-weeds/bathurst-burr|access-date=22 April 2012 |website=dpi.vic.gov.au}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=ITIS – Report: Acanthoxanthium spinosum|url=https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=508250#null|access-date=2021-12-27|website=www.itis.gov}}</ref> This species is part of the genus ''Xanthium'' that encompasses 25 different species of flowering plants of the daisy family, Asteraceae, and sunflower tribe.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Amin|first1=Surriya|last2=Khan|first2=Haroon|date=2016-05-04|title=Revival of Natural Products: Utilization of Modern Technologies|url=http://www.eurekaselect.com/openurl/content.php?genre=article&issn=1573-4072&volume=12&issue=2&spage=103|journal=Current Bioactive Compounds|language=en|volume=12|issue=2|pages=103–106|doi=10.2174/1573407212666160314195845|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Distribution==
It is known worldwide as a [[noxious weed]] that grows in many types of disturbed habitats such as pastures, crops, waterways, grasslands, flood plains, waste areas, and sometimes tropical and arid environments.<ref name=":0"/> Its original native range is not known but it may have come from [[South America]],<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242417494 Flora of North America]</ref> possibly from [[Chile]].<ref name="wa">[http://www.nwcb.wa.gov/weed_info/Written_findings/Xanthium_spinosum.html Washington State Noxious Weed Control Board] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724090157/http://www.nwcb.wa.gov/weed_info/Written_findings/Xanthium_spinosum.html|date=July 24, 2011}}</ref>  The plant is found in various regions across the world including Canada, the US, Central America, parts of Africa and the Middle East, China, Russia and Australia.<ref name=":4" />

==Description==
[[File:Xanthium spinosum sl25.jpg|thumb|Burs of ''Xanthium spinosum'']]
''Xanthium spinosum'' is an upright, highly branched, dichotomous, annual herb producing a slender stem up to {{convert|1|m}} tall or slightly taller. It is lined at intervals with very long, sharp, yellowish, three pronged [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|spines]] which may exceed three centimeters in length. These spines are typically found at the base of each leaf fork.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Sutherland|first=Steve|date=2004|title=Fuels planning: science synthesis and integration; environmental consequences fact sheet 07: fire and weeds|location=Ft. Collins, CO|doi=10.2737/rmrs-rn-23-v7|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The leaves are irregularly lobed or lance-shaped lobed, the middle is much longer than the others, and have white veins down the center.<ref name=":1" /> They are arranged spirally or alternately along the stem. Each is up to 10 or 12 centimeters long and are dark green or grayish on top, pale green or whitish underneath and are covered in downy hairs.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

''Xanthium spinosum'' flowers between summer and late fall, typically from July to October in the northern hemisphere. The plant produces male and female [[Head (botany)|flower heads]]  that are monoecious and form greenish axillary or solitary inflorescence clusters. The male flowers are bulbous and found in dense clusters at the tips of stems near the topmost leaves.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/56863#todescription|title=Xanthium spinosum|last=|first=|date=|website=CABI|access-date=2020-04-27}}</ref> Female flowers are found at the leaf forks on lower leaves and develop into burs.<ref name=":4" /> The [[bur]]s are one or 1.5 centimeters long and covered in small hook-like spines. Each bur has two seeds inside it that are flattened and have a thick coat.<ref name=":4" /> The spiny burs are easily [[Biological dispersal|dispersed]] to new areas when they become attached to animals, people, and objects, or float on water. [[File:Xanthium spinosum sl18.jpg|thumb|''Xanthium spinosum'' plant with lobed leaves and white stripe down the middle]]

==Uses==
''Xanthium spinosum'', as well as others within the genus, are used in many traditional medicinal treatments. The chloroform extracts found in the plant are used to treat numerous ailments such as hydrophobia, rabies, fevers, diarrhea, and cancer.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last1=Romero|first1=M.|last2=Zanuy|first2=M.|last3=Rosell|first3=E.|last4=Cascante|first4=M.|last5=Piulats|first5=J.|last6=Font-Bardia|first6=M.|last7=Balzarini|first7=J.|last8=De Clerq|first8=E.|last9=Pujol|first9=M.D.|date=January 2015|title=Optimization of xanthatin extraction from Xanthium spinosum L. and its cytotoxic, anti-angiogenesis and antiviral properties|journal=European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry|language=en|volume=90|pages=491–496|doi=10.1016/j.ejmech.2014.11.060|pmid=25481815|pmc=7115430}}</ref> In Chinese medicinal practices, the methanol extracts found in the leaves and fruits are used to treat inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis.<ref name=":2" /> This species can also be toxic to humans, as it produces toxins that cause nephrotoxic effects, causing damage to the kidneys.<ref name=":0" />

==Agricultural & ecological effects==
''Xanthium spinosum'' is classified as an invasive weed of many crops. This plant negatively impacts crops such as: cotton, maize, sunflowers, tomatoes, soybeans, sugarcane, and other annual or perennial crops.<ref name=":4" /> It decreases the health of the ecosystem it takes over and threatens the loss of the native species that inhabit the area as well as lowers the biodiversity.<ref name=":4" /> It also threatens the health and well being of the animals that inhabit the areas where it is found. If livestock ingests ''Xanthium spinosum'', the livestock will become poisoned and could potentially make its way into a human. The plants, especially new seedlings, are [[Toxin|toxic]] to [[livestock]].<ref name="wa" /> This plant is also toxic to humans.

Bur damage to [[sheep]]'s [[wool]] reduces its value.<ref name="wa" />
